Search cyclic signed-permutation orbit families (five 12-orbits plus one 8-orbit) over only six seed vectors with log-sum-exp L-BFGS, then release symmetry and basin-hop with momentum quenches plus trust-region LP polishing.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained families, then break the symmetry: generate configurations as unions of orbits of a finite group acting on $\mathbb{R}^{12}$, e.g. the group generated by a 12-cycle coordinate permutation and independent sign flips of coordinate blocks, giving generic orbits of size 12 — take five such orbits (60 points) plus one orbit of size 8 under a block-permutation subgroup, totalling 68. Optimise only the 6–7 seed vectors (each 11 degrees of freedom) with log-sum-exp plus LP restricted to seed parameters, scan several group choices and seed initialisations, then release all 68 points and LP-polish; even if the symmetric optimum is slightly worse, its released descendant lies in a different contact topology from the record basin.

idea: Cooperative worst-core descent attacking the isolated maximal pair with subset smooth-max L-BFGS, fast annealed repulsion basin hops and trust-region LP squeezing.

De novo basin census from Gaussian, Sobol, D12-lattice and greedy-maximin starts with short 30→300 log-sum-exp anneals, eigenvalue plus top-200 fingerprint de-duplication, then LP-polish of several dissimilar finalists.
direction: Run a genuinely de novo, diversity-preserving basin census that never loads `best.npy` until the final comparison: launch many cheap independent starts (random Gaussian, Sobol-on-sphere, $D_{12}$-lattice normalised integer vectors with entries in $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, and greedy maximin selections from those pools), anneal each for only 200–600 steps ($\beta=30\to300$ power/log-sum-exp), fingerprint survivors by sorted Gram-matrix eigenvalues and the sorted list of the top 200 pair cosines, and keep at most one representative per fingerprint cluster. Spend the remaining time LP-polishing the best few *dissimilar* finalists rather than the single best cheap score, returning the overall winner — this tests whether a structurally different basin beats the inherited record basin at all.

idea: Multi-point contact-load surgery deleting 3-8 jammed points and jointly re-optimising them from dense 50k hole search with staged log-sum-exp L-BFGS plus LP squeeze.
direction: Perform multi-point topology surgery instead of the single-point hole moves already tried: each iteration, rank points by contact load $\sum_j \exp(300(<x_i,x_j>-m))$, delete a random subset of $k\in\{3,4,5,6,8\}$ high-load points (sometimes a point plus its near-contact neighbours), and jointly re-optimise all $k$ deleted points against the frozen core and each other with the single/multi-point log-sum-exp L-BFGS ($\beta=100\to600$), initialised from a dense hole search ($50\,000$ random sphere candidates scored against the core, top 20 refined). Accept only if the subsequent 5–10 s LP polish beats the incumbent; this changes several contact-graph edges simultaneously and can move a cluster that no one-point relocation can unlock.

idea: Search 4x17 cyclic block-rotation families and optimize only seed variables with symmetric LSE gradients.
direction: Search the untried $4\times17$ cyclic symmetry, exploiting $68=4\cdot17$ and $12=6$ rotation planes. Let $C_{17}$ act by block-diagonal rotations through angles $2\pi m_jk/17$, $k=0,\ldots,16$, in the six coordinate planes, generate four full 17-orbits from four unit seed vectors, and enumerate or randomly sample multiplier sets $(m_1,\ldots,m_6)$ modulo $17$, sign changes, and permutation. Optimise only the $4\times12$ seed variables with analytic log-sum-exp L-BFGS at $\beta=100,300,1000,3000$, back-propagating the full gradient by averaging each orbit's tangent gradients back to its seed; finish with a symmetry-preserving LP in which displacements are orbit-averaged, and only release the symmetry for a final LP if the symmetric score is within $5\times10^{-4}$ of the incumbent. Try roughly 20 multiplier/seed combinations in the first 120 seconds, polish the best two, and return the incumbent if none improves it.

idea: Decreasing-threshold hinge feasibility with L-BFGS to break the jammed contact set, then LP squeeze.
direction: Replace direct minimisation of the maximum by a decreasing-threshold feasibility method designed to destroy the over-complete contact set and create slack/rattlers. For a target $\tau$, minimise $F_\tau=\sum_{i<j}\max(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau,0)^2$ by L-BFGS with its analytic gradient (zero gradient for pairs below $\tau$), starting from the incumbent and from tangent perturbations of size $0.01$--$0.05$; use targets $\tau=0.2198,0.2195,0.2192,0.2188,0.2184$, lowering $\tau$ whenever feasibility $\max_{i<j}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\le\tau$ is reached and re-perturbing whenever it stalls. This objective deliberately ignores already-safe pairs, so the optimiser can rearrange the active graph instead of equalising hundreds of contacts at once. After the lowest feasible $\tau$, run the usual LP polish; track contact counts and accept a basin as interesting if its mean contacts/point falls toward $11$--$13$ even before the final squeeze.

idea: Large cap surgery deleting 14-22 nearest neighbours, greedy refill from 200k pool, staged subset L-BFGS plus full anneal and LP polish cycling over distinct seeds.
direction: Perform macro-cluster surgery instead of the previously tried deletion of only 3--8 high-load points. Repeatedly choose a seed point and delete a contiguous block of 14--22 points consisting of its nearest neighbours in cosine, equivalently a spectral community of the contact graph or a cap in the top principal components, freeze the remaining 46--54 points, and refill the hole from a 200,000-point Gaussian/Sobol candidate pool by greedy minimisation of the maximum dot product against the frozen core and already inserted points. Then optimise the inserted points jointly against the frozen core with staged log-sum-exp L-BFGS ($\beta=100,300,900$), unfreeze all 68 points for a short anneal, and LP-polish; cycle through several geographically distinct clusters. This changes a whole neighbourhood topology at once, which small rattler-style surgery cannot do in a configuration with no rattlers.

idea: Break the over-jammed basin with large topology-changing kicks and hinge-feasibility hops targeting a threshold below the incumbent, followed by smooth minimax re-polish and multi-hole reinsertion.
Anisotropic-metric homotopy with fingerprint anti-return deflation to leave the over-jammed basin.
direction: Use an anisotropic-metric homotopy with explicit anti-return deflation to leave the incumbent basin without deleting points. Sample a random orthogonal $Q$ and exponents $\epsilon_j\in[-0.35,0.35]$, form $D=Q\,\mathrm{diag}(e^{\epsilon_j})Q^{T}$, transform $y_i=D^{1/2}x_i/\lVert D^{1/2}x_i\rVert$, and optimise the spherical code in the $y$ variables (equivalently under the deformed inner product $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle_D$), then follow a six-step path $\epsilon\to0$, re-optimising with log-sum-exp L-BFGS and a short LP at each step before mapping back and normalising. Run about eight such paths from the incumbent and from random starts, but reject any endpoint whose sorted top-200 inner-product fingerprint is within $10^{-4}$ in $L^2$ of the incumbent, since that is the same basin; LP-polish only fingerprint-distinct endpoints and keep the global best as a fallback.

idea: Escape the over-jammed LP vertex by rupture-and-repair basin hops that delete the worst contact clique, reinsert points in large holes, then re-anneal with low-to-high log-sum-exp L-BFGS and short LP squeezes.

Incumbent-free diverse population search with low-discrepancy, lattice-jitter and farthest-point starts optimized by stable p-mean Riesz stages then high-beta log-sum-exp, histogram-clustered basin archive and Procrustes-matched recombination with final LP squeeze.
direction: Run a genuinely incumbent-free global population search: generate many random, low-discrepancy, and perturbed-lattice initial configurations, optimize them first with Riesz or positive-part power potentials using exponents $p=8,16,32,64,128$ and only then with high-beta minimax log-sum-exp, and maintain an archive clustered by sorted pairwise-cosine histograms and contact-graph fingerprints so that near-duplicates of the known basin are discarded even if their scores are good. Promote several distinct basins through longer anneals, recombine configurations only after optimal rotational alignment and point matching, and use the loaded record solely as a final comparison rather than as a seed, thereby testing whether an entirely different contact topology can beat the current rigid graph.

idea: Delete-and-reinsert surgery manufacturing rattlers with massive hole search, greedy reinsertion, hinge targeting on inserts and full LSE release with topology-diverse acceptance.
direction: Perform deliberate delete-and-reinsert surgery that manufactures rattlers: repeatedly choose $k\in\{2,\ldots,8\}$ points for removal, biased toward points with 24–28 contacts, points participating in the tightest cliques, and occasional random or spatially clustered subsets; freeze the remaining $68-k$ points, generate at least $2\times10^5$ random spherical hole candidates, rank them by their maximum cosine to the frozen set, locally refine the best 30 as one-point insertions, and greedily insert the removed points one at a time. Then optimize only the inserted points with a hinge objective targeting cosines below the incumbent by margins such as $5\times10^{-5}$ and $2\times10^{-4}$, followed by a full log-sum-exp release with beta increasing from about 100 to 10000, reserving LP polishing for the final few seconds and accepting candidates whose contact adjacency differs substantially from the incumbent, not merely candidates with an immediately better score.

idea: Build quantized 12D pools (756 Coxeter-Todd vectors via Eisenstein/hexacode lift plus D12 roots and 4096-cube) and select 68 points by decreasing-threshold violation repair / simulated-annealing swaps, then release the best discrete subsets with soft-max descent and trust-region LP.
direction: Search discrete algebraic candidate pools before continuous optimization: construct large normalized pools from highly structured 12D configurations, most importantly the 756 minimal vectors of the Coxeter–Todd lattice $K_{12}$ if generated via its Eisenstein-integer/hexacode construction, supplemented by $D_{12}$ roots and other lattice shells, then formulate selection of 68 pool points as a minimax combinatorial problem and solve it with greedy violation repair, simulated-annealing swaps, and tabu moves that replace points involved in pairs above thresholds decreasing from about $0.25$ toward $0.21$. Any 68-point subset whose discrete maximum is competitive should then be continuously released with log-sum-exp and LP polishing; this directly seeks the quantized, symmetry-rich structure missing from the current amorphous solution rather than perturbing that solution.

idea: Escape the over-jammed vertex with simulated-annealing dense-subgraph surgery that deletes contact-dense clusters (not geometric caps) and jointly re-optimizes the hole with farthest-point refill plus sideways moves.
Destroy-and-repair basin hopping on overloaded clusters with joint subset log-sum-exp re-optimization to force contact-topology changes.
